title: A home final, but where?
text: The Cats have earned a home final, and the league says Kardinia Park is too small: it wants the game at the MCG. The coach's word will be quoted either way.

choices.label: Fight for Kardinia Park in the press

effects.hit_result: The league gives way. The final is at Kardinia Park.
effects.miss_result: The final stays at the 'G, and the league remembers the fight.

choices.result: The town is right behind the coach.

choices.label: "We'll play anywhere."

effects.why: Members who can't get a seat at the 'G felt let down

choices.result: The league and the neutral press like it. Members who can't get a seat at the 'G feel let down.

choices.label: Ask the club to buy members' tickets at the 'G

effects.why: The club got its members into the final

choices.result: The Geelong faithful fill one end. It costs real money.

title: Only good at home?
text: The Cats won well at Kardinia Park and lost on the road again. A Melbourne commentator calls them flat-track bullies who need their narrow home ground to win. Next week is away.

choices.label: Train on a full-width ground all week
choices.result: The players get used to the space. The bus trip every day takes it out of them.

choices.label: Pin the quote up
choices.result: The group wants to prove him wrong. They might press too hard early.

choices.label: "Our ground, our advantage."
choices.result: The group stays relaxed. The tag sticks in the press.

title: The bridesmaids
text: Close again, and no flag again. Every paper has the same word for Geelong on Monday: bridesmaids. The board wants to know how the coach will answer it over summer.

choices.label: Wear it yourself at the press conference
choices.result: The players are shielded from the tag. The coach becomes the face of it.

choices.label: "This group will win one."

effects.why: The coach backed the group to win one

effects.hit_result: The board starts asking whether the group has another one in it.

choices.result: The players feel backed. If they fall short again, it's on the coach.

choices.label: Freshen the list: move on two senior players

effects.why: The club moved on senior players to find new hunger

choices.result: New blood and more games for the kids. The senior group is shaken and the members lose two favourites.

title: The number on the banner
text: The cheer squad wants this week's banner to carry the number of years since the last premiership. Half the members think it's a rallying cry; the other half think it's a jinx.

choices.label: "Put it up."
choices.result: The players run through the number. They feel what a flag would mean, and the weight of it.

choices.label: "Leave the number off."
choices.result: The group plays light. Some supporters reckon the club is ducking its history.

title: Coming home to the Barwon
text: A Geelong-born star at another club wants to come home. His manager says he'll take less to wear the hoops, but his club wants a high pick for him.

choices.label: Pay the price: our first pick

effects.why: The club paid to bring a local star home

choices.result: A proven player who wants to be here. No top young talent arrives this year.

choices.label: Offer a lesser deal and wait

effects.hit_result: His club blinks, and he comes home.
effects.miss_result: His club calls the bluff, and he stays put.

choices.result: The pick stays, and the phone calls go back and forth.

choices.label: Wait until his contract runs out

effects.why: The club held its nerve on the price

effects.hit_result: Another club gets in first, and the town wonders why the Cats waited.

choices.result: It costs nothing now. Another club could outbid the Cats in the meantime.

title: The local boy or the interstater
text: With the first pick, the recruiters rate an interstate teenager slightly higher. The local favourite is a Geelong boy whose family have been members for decades.

choices.label: Take the local boy

effects.why: The club took the lower-rated local boy

choices.result: He's settled and won't want to leave. The recruiters rated the other kid higher.

choices.label: Take the interstater

effects.why: The recruiters got the player they rated highest

choices.result: The higher-rated talent arrives. The town wanted its own boy, and he may want to go home one day.

title: The state league find
text: The recruiters love a 24-year-old who has been best on ground every week in the state league. He's ready now. The other option with the same pick is a teenager who might be better in five years.

choices.label: Take the mature-age player

effects.why: The club picked a player ready for senior footy now

choices.result: He's ready for senior footy now. His ceiling is lower and his career shorter.

choices.label: Take the teenager
choices.result: Long-term upside. The board wanted help now.

title: Rest the old boys?
text: Three of the most experienced players are sore after a hard month. It's a short trip and a winnable game. The veterans want to play; the fitness staff want them in the stands.

choices.label: Rest all three
choices.result: The legs will be fresh for the run home. The veterans hate watching.

choices.label: Play them
choices.result: The best side takes the field. The old legs are grinding down.

choices.label: Rest one, play two

effects.hit_result: The two who played are feeling it.

choices.result: A middle path. No one is fully happy.

title: One more crack
text: The side is a contender. The list manager can trade next year's first-round pick for an established player ready to slot straight in. The board asks the coach: win now, or protect the future?

choices.label: Trade the pick

effects.why: The club went all in for another flag

choices.result: A stronger side right now. Fewer kids are coming through.

choices.label: Keep the pick

effects.why: The club kept its pipeline full

choices.result: The pipeline stays full. The senior players think the coach blinked.

title: Hawks week
text: Hawthorn next. Neither club's supporters have to be told why it matters, and the players want a big week.

choices.label: Make it a big week
choices.result: The group lifts. Training runs hot all week.

choices.label: "Just another four points."
choices.result: Fresh legs and clear heads. The supporters wanted fire.

title: The pact
text: {opp}'s president has told the press the Cats lack the mental toughness to bounce back. The leadership group wants to make a private vow in the rooms: never lose to this club again.

choices.label: Let them make the pact
choices.result: The vow is made behind closed doors. Lose to them now and it will hurt.

choices.label: Keep it on our own game

effects.why: The coach kept the group on its own game

choices.result: No extra weight. The leaders feel held back.

choices.label: Answer him in the press
choices.result: The supporters love it. {opp}'s players read it too, and they come out firing.

title: A one-paper town
text: The local paper covers the Cats every day, front and back, and its chief football writer wants a sit-down on the list's future. The Melbourne papers want the same interview first.

choices.label: Give it to the local paper
choices.result: The town hears it first. The Melbourne press goes after the side all week.

choices.label: Give it to the Melbourne papers

hit.why: The local paper turned on the club after a snub

effects.hit_result: The local paper feels snubbed, and Saturday's story is a hard one.

choices.result: Bigger reach, and recruits read it.

choices.label: No interviews this week
choices.result: The coach's week stays on the footy. Both papers are annoyed.

title: Live in Geelong
text: A handful of players commute from Melbourne every day, over an hour each way. The leaders want a club rule: if you play for Geelong, you live in Geelong.

choices.label: Make it a rule

effects.why: The whole group lives in the town it plays for

effects.hit_result: A player with a partner in Melbourne starts talking about a trade.

choices.result: The group lives and trains as one, with more time to recover.

choices.label: Encourage it, don't force it

effects.why: Most of the group moved down the highway

choices.result: No one is upset. The commuters stay tired.

choices.label: Leave it to the players

effects.why: The leaders felt overruled

choices.result: The players' private lives stay theirs. The leaders feel overruled.

title: A big employer closes
text: One of the region's biggest factories is shutting, and hundreds of families in the club's heartland are losing work. The town wants the club to do something.

choices.label: Free memberships for the families

effects.why: The club stood with the town when the factory shut

choices.result: The town knows the club stands with it. It costs real money.

choices.label: The players visit the workers

effects.why: The players met the town they play for

choices.result: The players see the town they play for. It comes out of the training week.

choices.label: A statement and a match-day collection

hit.why: Some in town said the club did too little

effects.hit_result: Some in town say it wasn't enough.

choices.result: Something done, at little cost.

title: Sandhills on the Surf Coast
text: The fitness staff want a week on the dunes and beaches down the Surf Coast. The skills coaches want the time on the track.

choices.label: A week on the sand

effects.why: The group suffered through the sandhills together

effects.hit_result: Sore calves are still there for the first game.

choices.result: The group bonds on the dunes. Fewer skill sessions get done.

choices.label: Stay at the club
choices.result: The skills sharpen. The group misses the getaway.

title: A new stand at Kardinia Park
text: The board wants to borrow to help build a new stand: more seats, better rooms. The football department's budget would be squeezed for three seasons.

choices.label: Back the stand
choices.result: Bigger crowds and better rooms are coming. The football department tightens its belt.

choices.label: Protect the football budget
choices.result: The list and the staff stay strong. The board is frustrated and the project slips.

title: The bank's letter
text: The club is deep in debt and the bank wants a plan. The board can sell a home game to a Melbourne ground, run a members' appeal, or cut the football department.

choices.label: Sell a home game to Melbourne

effects.why: The town lost a game at Kardinia Park

choices.result: A guaranteed cheque. The town loses a game at Kardinia Park.

choices.label: Run a members' appeal

hit.why: The town rallied to pay down the debt

effects.hit_result: The appeal hits its target, and the town is proud of it.
effects.miss_result: The appeal falls short, and the debt is in the paper every day.

choices.result: The town is asked to dig deep.

choices.label: Cut the football department
choices.result: The debt shrinks. Fewer staff means less development.

title: Son of a Cat
text: The son of a club great is old enough for the draft and can join his dad's old club. The recruiters think he's a middling prospect. The members, and his father, want him in the hoops.

choices.label: Take him

effects.why: A list spot went to a long shot

choices.result: The family and the members are delighted. The recruiters think it's a long shot.

choices.label: Pass on him

effects.why: The list spot went to the recruiters' pick

choices.result: The spot goes to the recruiters' pick. The family and the members are hurt.

title: The reserves want to win it
text: The reserves are pushing for the finals, and their coach wants the fringe senior players every week. The senior coaches want them rested and ready to come in.

choices.label: Play them in the reserves every week

effects.hit_result: The ones called up are tired by the time they're needed.

choices.result: Match fitness and a winning culture underneath the seniors.

choices.label: Give the spots to local league players

effects.why: Local players got their shot in the hoops

choices.result: The locals get a shot and the recruiters see more. The fringe players go cold.

title: A night on the waterfront
text: After a win, a group of Geelong players stayed out late at a waterfront bar, and a phone video is everywhere by morning. Nothing illegal, but in a town this size everybody saw it.

choices.label: Fines and a public apology

effects.why: The club made its standards public

choices.result: The standards are clear. The group feels hung out to dry.

choices.label: Handle it inside the club

effects.hit_result: More video comes out, and the board is not happy.

choices.result: The players trust the coach. The local paper calls it soft.

title: Taking unders
text: A star wants to join Geelong, and his manager says he'll take far less than his market value. Rival clubs are already whispering that there must be something else in it.

choices.label: Sign him on the cut-price deal

effects.hit_result: The league opens an investigation into the deal.

choices.result: A star at a bargain. The league may take a close look.

choices.label: Pay him what he's worth

effects.why: The club kept its books clean

choices.result: Clean books and nothing to hide. The cap is squeezed for everyone else.

choices.label: Walk away

effects.why: The list's pay stays fair for everyone

choices.result: No risk taken. The supporters wonder why.

title: Never bottom out
text: The side has fallen out of the eight with an ageing list. The board's line has always been that Geelong doesn't bottom out. Some members want a full rebuild; the board wants to reset on the run.

choices.label: Reset on the run

effects.why: The club refused to bottom out

effects.hit_result: The board wonders whether the old list has anything left.

choices.result: The side stays competitive. The ceiling may be lower.

choices.label: Rebuild properly
choices.result: A younger list and more games for the kids. Two or three hard seasons lie ahead.

title: A long way from home
text: {name} is struggling: no family nearby, few mates, and a quiet regional town. His manager says he's thinking about asking to go home.

choices.label: Move him in with a senior player's family

effects.why: The club found him a home and a mentor

choices.result: {name} has a home and a mentor. The senior player gives up his own time.

choices.label: Fly his family over for a week
choices.result: {name} feels looked after. It may not last.

choices.label: Give him time; he'll adjust

effects.why: No player got special treatment

choices.result: No favourites for anyone. {name} is still thinking about home.

title: A town in hoops
text: Every shop window in Geelong is blue and white, the schools have dress-up days, and the club has a hundred requests for player visits. The players love it, but it's the biggest week of their lives.

choices.label: Send the players into town
choices.result: The group feels the whole region behind it. Tired and a bit distracted.

choices.label: Lock the doors
choices.result: Total focus. The town feels shut out.

choices.label: One open session, then lock down
choices.result: A middle path. Neither full energy nor full rest.

title: Sold out
text: Kardinia Park sells out every week, and thousands are on the membership waitlist. Marketing wants to sell more memberships than there are seats, betting not everyone turns up.

choices.label: Sell past capacity

hit.why: Members were turned away on a big day

effects.hit_result: On the next big day, members are turned away at the gate.

choices.result: More money and more members.

choices.label: Hold the cap

effects.why: Every member gets a seat

choices.result: Every member gets a seat. The waitlist grows and the board misses the income.
